chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik and Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari both narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, Muhammad ibn Isa, and Abdullah ibn Aamir al-Qasabani all narrated to us, from Abdurrahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Musawir, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar al-Ju'fi, who said: I heard the Sheikh - meaning Abu Abdullah - saying:

Beware of allusion (or mention), for by Allah, he will be hidden for a period of time, and he will be neglected until it is said: He died, he perished, in which valley did he go? The eyes of the believers will shed tears for him, and he will be turned over like a ship in the waves of the sea, and no one will be saved except those whom Allah has taken a covenant from, and inscribed faith in their hearts, and strengthened them with a spirit from Him. And twelve ambiguous banners will be raised, and it will not be known which is from which. (He said) I cried, then I said to him: What shall we do? He said: O Abu Abdullah, then he looked at a sunbeam entering the porch: Do you see this sun? I said: Yes. He said: Our matter is clearer than this sun.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs and conditions of the Imam's occultation according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) foretells the Great Occultation, emphasizing that the Imam's true authority will remain evident despite the confusion of competing claims, likened to 'twelve ambiguous standards.' The scholar highlights the criterion for salvation as those upon whom God has written faith and strengthened with His spirit, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology. This narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the transition from the Minor to the Great Occultation and the enduring clarity of the Imam's guidance amidst societal turmoil.
